# Independent audit: ten-point diamond filter and exact coarse/fine depth gap



## Exact base and graph sources

The base hull Q'=conv(W) is contained in the already certified eleven-point lattice polytope. The old point p9 is outside because y+z=3 there and at most two on W. The only other old point absent from W is p2, which belongs to Q' by either of its two midpoint representations. Thus Q' has exactly the ten listed integer points P'.

The exposing table makes all nine W points vertices of Q'. Its only nonvertex integer point is p2, in the relative interior of the five-point diamond on y=0. Restriction of the previously proved Jensen height is legitimate because every representation using P' is also an original representation. Equivalently its affine formula on the diamond is the only nontrivial condition.

The integral graph removes exactly p2 at height 1/2. Its hull has no other integer points by projection to P' and Jensen affinity, so T'=W_hat is an actual nine-point lattice-convex subset of Z^4. The four affinely independent height-zero points and a height-one point prove full four-dimensional affine span. All its points are vertices.

## Exact Helly values

The five-point diamond has Helly number three. Three noncollinear corners supply the lower bound. Four corners have the center in every deletion triangle, while any four-point subset containing the center fails convex position because its three corners contain an opposite pair. No larger critical witness is possible. The finite-set union bound therefore gives h(P')<=3+5=8.

For the matching lower bound, V=W minus p3 has eight exposed points. The omitted p3 is outside conv(V) because every available y=0 point has z<=1. The center p2 is outside the deletion hull omitting p0: its y=0 sources are then only p1,p6, whose segment excludes p2. All other P' points are members of V and excluded by their own exposing deletion. Thus the eight deletion hulls have empty P' intersection and are critical. This proves h(P')=8. The nine graph vertices give h(T')=9 by the analogous deletion family and the trivial finite-cardinality upper bound.

## Full ambient dimension and intrinsic measures

For any full s-dimensional simplex K, the product conv(W_hat) times K has full ambient dimension 4+s. At every coarse integer base p in P', the u-fiber of the graph hull is the SINGLE value g(p); hence the coarse fiber is exactly {g(p)} times K. This is an s-dimensional isometric copy of K inside the s+1 continuous coordinates. All ten coarse fibers have H_s-volume V_K, while their full (s+1)-volumes vanish.

Imposing the additional integer condition u in Z retains precisely nine of these fibers, all positive and equal to K. Their total fine H_s mass is 9V_K, versus coarse intrinsic mass 10V_K. These are the respective Hausdorff dimensions and normalizations; there is no unmentioned point fiber or zero-mass outlier. The fine set contains every generating product vertex, so its convex hull is the complete ambient body.

## Exact fine depth for every ambient cap

At each W base, the integer exposing normal has gap at least one from every other W base. Thus the displayed margin

    lambda_r(x)-1/(s+1)+2 n_i dot(p-p_i)

is strictly negative on every other fine K fiber, since 0<=lambda_r<=1. On its own fiber it is exactly the canonical simplex cap. The s+1 such caps cover that entire fiber, each with mass Gamma_s V_K. Their union over all nine bases proves the global upper bound Gamma_s/9.

At any fine fiber centroid, every containing ambient closed halfspace restricts to a containing continuous halfspace or the whole simplex. The ordinary simplex centroid theorem therefore supplies the matching lower bound. This includes arbitrary coefficients of p and u and the x-normal-zero case. Hence the exact fine maximum is Gamma_s/9.

## Exact coarse depth and all closed-boundary cases

The newly eligible point a2 has base (p2,1/2) and continuous coordinate c_K. Within the y=0 facet, four other graph bases form two opposite pairs about it. For a cap through a2 with nonzero x-normal, each pair has opposite centroid thresholds in its two identical K fibers. The already independently audited paired-centroid-tail theorem gives at least 2Gamma_s V_K per pair, while the own fiber gives Gamma_s V_K. This totals 5Gamma_s V_K.

If the x-normal is zero, the closed cap contains the entire own fiber and at least one entire fiber of each opposite pair. Its mass is at least 3V_K>=5Gamma_s V_K, since s>=1 and Gamma_s<=1/2. A containing cap may be shifted to a through-point cap only by increasing its threshold, so this reduction decreases mass and has the correct direction. Thus depth_coarse(a2)>=Gamma_s/2.

For the upper bound on every point of the p2 fiber, the canonical caps with margin `lambda_r(x)-1/(s+1)-2y` capture exactly the same simplex cap in each of the five y=0 fibers and exclude all other fibers strictly. Each has mass 5Gamma_s V_K, and they cover the p2 fiber.

For any other coarse base p_i, at least one of the two disjoint midpoint pairs omits p_i. Consequently p2 lies in conv(W minus p_i), and the original exposing gap remains at least one against this extra coarse point. The same isolating simplex caps give upper depth Gamma_s/10 at every such point. There are no further coarse bases. Therefore the global coarse maximum is exactly Gamma_s/2 and is attained at a2.

The ratio of the two maxima is exactly 2/9. The constant comparison Gamma_s/9<Gamma_(s+1)/8 for s>=2 can also be checked without a further dependency: the function q log(q/(q+1)) has second derivative 1/[q(q+1)^2]>0 for q>0, so consecutive Gamma ratios strictly increase from Gamma_2/Gamma_1=8/9. Equality holds at s=1. The actual fine OC target remains Gamma_s/16, strictly below the certified fine maximum.

All lattices, intrinsic masses, affine dimensions, and ambient closed-halfspace cases pass.
